attributes.documentation: EXFOR No. = 30775.002. Journal article = Boldeman et al., Nuclear Science and Engineering, Vol.93, p.181 (1986). The data by Boldeman~\emph{et al.} \cite{Boldeman_1986} appear in EXFOR sub-entries 30775.003 ($^6$Li, $E_\mathrm{out} <$  3 MeV) and 30775.002 (liquid scintillator, $E_\mathrm{out} >$ 1 MeV. Mannhart mean values agreeing with EXFOR mean values, except for 6 data points around the $^6$Li peak, the highest two data points of sub-entry 30775.003 and 3 unspecified data points of 30775.002. This work summarized eight experiments to measure the $^{252}$Cf PFNS: seven measurements using a 5.08~cm diameter times 2.54~cm thick NE-102 plastic scintillator with lower energy limits ranging from 1.0-2.0~MeV and upper limits from 13.7--14.7~MeV, and one measurement using a 5.08~cm diameter $	imes$ 2.0~mm thick Li-glass detector over 0.124--2.660~MeV energy limits.  NE-102 and Li-glass measurements were made with neutron flight paths of 0.40 and 3.015~m, respectively.  Fission events were measured with a methane-filled parallel-plate avalanche counter (PPAC).  The PPAC efficiency for fragment detection was measured with a Marion counter.  No collimation was used between the PPAC and the neutron detector in order to avoid scattering off of the collimator itself.  Measurements were made with a raised, 5 m high experiment area in order to avoid neutron scattering from the floor, with a 90 mm shadow bar used for NE-102 measurements only. Corrections for detector dead time, air attenuation, delayed neutrons and $\gamma$ rays, air-scattered neutrons, timing resolution, and fission fragment loss below threshold were all included in the analysis, with a thorough discussion.  The seven NE-102 measurements are combined to form a single result, and are reported combined with the Li-glass results.  The results are noted to compare reasonably well with a 1.42~MeV Maxwellian, but show notable and energy-dependent shape deviations from this trend.  The broad peak in the Li-glass data about a centroid of approximately 240~keV with a sharp drop from 300--400~keV and a slow rise to near unity, relative to a 1.42~MeV Maxwellian, are perhaps the most notable features.  Data from 1.0--5.0~MeV show a roughly flat ratio slightly above unity within statistics relative to the same Maxwellian, followed by a slow decline to a ratio of approximately 0.9 at 10~MeV.  These features of the NE-102 data agree with other measurements in the same ranges.  Data above 10~MeV vary between Maxwellian ratios of 0.754 and 1.072, but with large uncertainties. Unfortunately, no detailed partial uncertainties are provided. Statistical and total uncertaintites are ver similar given in the EXFOR entry, which is unrealistic. I assume 10% of the deadtime correction as unc., and other unc. (background, multiple scattering, and detector efficiency unc., etc.) using templates. The NE-102 scintillator efficiency was measured with the associated particle method at a Van de Graaff accelerator.  There was no mention of keeping the experimental environment the same as in the PFNS measurement, though at high outgoing energies this is likely not an issue.  The definition of ``high outgoing energies'' depends on the experimental environment involved.  On the other hand, the Li-glass efficiency measurement, also measured at a Van de Graaff accelerator, was explicitly stated to be as close to identical to the PFNS measurement as possible.  This statement was likely a reflection of the increased effect from neutron scattering expected for lower outgoing neutron energies.  The Li-glass data also show suspicious features resembling the $^6$Li($n$,$t$) resonance near 240~keV and a sharp decline above this resonance.  The NE-102 data also show some structure in the 1--5~MeV range, but this is only within 1--2\%.  Lastly, a 1.07~MeV Maxwellian was ``folded''. Similar to Mannhart, we reject Li-glass data points of Boldeman with structures related to the $^6$Li($n$,$t$) reaction itself.  The NE-102 data were accepted for this evaluation.
Author: Boldeman
